instruction: Enable the Chrome Refresh Themed Realbox flag in Chrome's experimental features.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent navigated to chrome://flags and searched for 'refresh', 'ChromeRefresh2023', and 'modern'. Found some refresh-related flags when searching 'refresh' but did not find or enable the target flags. Gave up after 11 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate to chrome://flags, use the search box to filter flags, type URLs in address bar, interact with Chrome UI elements
metadata.failure_analysis: The target flags chrome-refresh-2023 and chrome-webui-refresh-2023 do not exist in Chrome 130. The model searched with correct intent but wrong flag names. It found related flags (ntp-realbox-cr23-theming, pdf-cr23) but did not attempt to change any dropdown values.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to enabling a single flag (ntp-realbox-cr23-theming) that was actually visible in the trajectory when model searched 'refresh'. Tests the same flag-modification capability at reduced complexity.
metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating to chrome://flags, searching for the Chrome Refresh Themed Realbox flag, and enabling it. Evaluator restarts Chrome and checks enabled experiments include ntp-realbox-cr23-theming.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads Chrome's Local State file to extract browser.enabled_labs_experiments list, which is the right state for verifying enabled flags.
Metric check_enabled_experiments correctly receives the rules dict directly (type='rule' handling is correct) and accesses rule['type'] and rule['names'].
Expected flag name 'ntp-realbox-cr23-theming' matches the flag observed in the trajectory, confirming it exists in this Chrome version.
Postconfig appropriately kills and restarts Chrome to ensure Local State is flushed to disk before the getter reads it.

Minor concern: check_enabled_experiments uses exact list equality (==) rather than a subset/contains check. If any other experiments are pre-enabled in the VM snapshot, the evaluator would incorrectly return 0.0 even if the target flag IS enabled. This is fragile but likely works on a clean snapshot.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider using a subset check (all names in enabled list) instead of exact equality, to avoid false negatives when other experiments are pre-enabled. However, since this is an existing OSWorld metric function, this is a known design choice and may be intentional for the clean VM context.
